- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (0.0), model often overestimates near-term upside — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85), model frequently overcorrects or overshoots — cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or adjust downward after 2–3 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in early 30d horizon — add 3–5% bias upward for first 5–7 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model exhibits mean-reversion bias — forecast should be slightly above recent 5-day average to avoid underestimating volatility.  
- When true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >90+ for 3+ consecutive days), model often lags — adjust forecast to match trend 1–2 days ahead.  
- If sentiment history includes 0.33 (strong bullish), model often fails to capture full rally — increase forecast by 2–5% for first 3–5 days of 30d horizon.
